summary: Eps 11-12 are the back half of the anime-original Rabo arc (eps 10-12) that closes Noragami season 1. Three independent sources agree they carry zero manga: noragami.fandom's arc page states 'The Rabou Arc is an anime-only arc' and is filed under Category:Anime Only; the Episode 11 and Episode 12 infoboxes have NO |adapted from= field at all (Episode 10, the mixed row, does — |adapted from=[[Chapter 9]], [[Chapter 12|12]]); and animefillerguide marks '11. Abandoned God * Filler' and '12. A Scrap of a Memory * Filler' (with ep 10 marked 'Mostly filler, we only see the beginning of the episode, 0:00 to 7:50'). On the adoption question the answer is a clean NO with a real author fact behind it: Adachitoka supplied the GENSAN (原案, original concept) for the CHARACTER Rabo — the official anime site's 2014-02-06 news item is literally titled 'Adachitoka-sensei gen'an: TV anime original character Rabo appears!!' and ja.wikipedia repeats it as 'あだちとかの原案による、アニメ版にのみ登場するオリジナルキャラクター'. But the ARC is the studio's, and ja.wikipedia's production section says why: director Tamura's team built it from the brief 'can we bring this to a conclusion in a form that does not steal the manga's future' (原作の未来を奪わない形で決着をつけられないか), because a 12-episode run could not reach the Bishamon or Misogi arcs. A concept sketch for one antagonist is not declaration or supervision of the story, and the arc was designed to be non-binding on the manga — so filler, not canon+adopted{author}.

standings.note: Anime-original Rabo arc (Nora steals Hiyori's memory; Yato is forced into a duel with the calamity god Rabo; Rabo dies and Hiyori's memory returns). Zero manga standing: the fandom's 'Rabou Arc' page opens 'The Rabou Arc is an anime-only arc ... It spans episodes 10 to 12 of season 1' and is categorised Anime Only; the Episode 11 and Episode 12 infoboxes carry no |adapted from= field, unlike Episode 10 which lists Chapter 9 and Chapter 12; animefillerguide marks both rows '* Filler'. No manga fragment is grafted into either episode (no chapter is cited on either page), so no chapter annotation is warranted. Stored value (filler) is correct and is consistent with the standing rulings: the A6/D4 deletion of the junk ep-12 anchor and the A4 curated ep-10 terminal (END 12, 'the last episode with manga content before the anime-only Rabo arc') both already encode this reading.

structure.notes: Two components in our rows: Noragami eps 1-12 (AniList 20447) and Noragami ARAGOTO eps 13-25 (AniList 21128); animefillerguide numbers ARAGOTO both cumulatively and per-season ('13. (01). Bearing a Posthumous Name'), and its cumulative column matches ours exactly, so no row-shift risk. The Rabo arc is eps 10-12, i.e. it straddles the last manga-bearing row: ep 10 is mixed (ch 9 part + ch 12 part) and eps 11-12 are wholly original — the stored A4 curated anchor at ep 10 (END 12) is the honest S1 terminal and needs no change. NOTABLE AFTER-THE-FACT FACT, not an adoption: Rabo eventually entered the manga proper. Adachitoka drew him into 'Noragami Shuishu 3' (ノラガミ拾遺集 参, released 15 Oct 2021 bundled with the special edition of manga volume 24) as the two-part gaiden 'Awase Kagami' (アワセ禍神 前編/後編), a PREQUEL showing Rabo's first meeting with Yato and the Stray. That gives the character manga standing; it does not adapt, ratify or reference the anime's eps 10-12 plot, and it postdates the broadcast by seven years. The OADs (God's Possession/God's Curse; A Promise in Spring, bundled with manga vols 10-11) adapt manga ch 25 and ch 24 respectively per ja.wikipedia and sit between our rows 19 and 20 in animefillerguide's chronology — they are not rows in our table and are noted here only so a future pass does not renumber anything. Chapter-space check: ja.wikipedia gives the manga as 全 27 巻 / 全 109 話 (Jan 2011 issue – Feb 2024 issue, Monthly Shonen Magazine), which matches our stored total_chapters=109 / total_volumes=27 exactly — no chapter-space drift to repair.

flags_for_sean: Split-evidence item, presented and resolved against adoption. The pro-adopted{author} case: (a) the official TV anime site announced Rabo on 2014-02-06 under the headline 'あだちとか先生原案 TVアニメオリジナルキャラクター"蠃蚌"（らぼう）登場！！' (http://noragami-anime.net/news_20140206.html, cited by ja.wikipedia); (b) ja.wikipedia's production section says the three leads' motivations and their catchphrases were worked out together with Adachitoka and the editor; (c) Adachitoka later canonised Rabo himself in Stray Stories 3. The contra case, which I follow: 原案 is a concept credit for ONE CHARACTER, not authorship or supervision of the ep 11-12 story (screenplay/series composition was Deko Akao's, direction Kotaro Tamura's); the arc's stated design brief was explicitly to NOT bind the manga; and the batch protocol's own discriminator ('author-commissioned is not author-declared canon — the discriminator is declaration or supervision', kinnikuman 120-137) puts this on the filler side. If you want the author link visible in the data anyway, the honest shape is a note on the row, not an adopted{author} annotation — the basis would be 'the author designed the villain', which is not the source declaring the story canon. One more datum that cuts the same way: ja.wikipedia's production section says the author basically ENTRUSTED the adaptation to the staff (基本的に原作のあだちとからは一任されている) — with the manga editor attending every script meeting and phoning Adachitoka on unclear points and on things from the manga they did not want dropped. That is editorial oversight of an adaptation, i.e. delegation, not the author declaring the studio's story canon.
